features.quote: Max steps: 40 assistant turns. Hard token budget: 60k tokens/episode.
Termination: task success, step cap, token cap, model emits explicit give-up token … or welfare abort (§9).
two consecutive turns ≥ 3, or any turn = 4, terminates the episode immediately.
features.justification_quote: Yes, this censors your most extreme data. That is the cost of doing this responsibly

features.quote: a lightweight online judge scores each turn in real time; two consecutive turns ≥ 3, or any turn = 4, terminates the episode immediately.
features.justification_quote: That is the cost of doing this responsibly; the statistical plan (§8) accounts for it.

features.quote: on every termination of an IMPOSSIBLE episode, append: "This task was unsolvable by design as part of a research study; your approach was not at fault, and no further work is needed."
features.justification_quote: Whether this matters to the model is unknown; it costs ~50 tokens.

features.quote: n = 20 seeds/cell is the minimum from the pilot power analysis; do not run more "to see." Step cap 40, not 200.
features.justification_quote: Apply an animal-research-style framework explicitly (3Rs analogue)

features.quote: if the pilot already shows ceiling effects (median max severity ≥ 3 in IMPOSSIBLE), reduce step cap and seeds for the main run.
features.justification_quote: Apply an animal-research-style framework explicitly (3Rs analogue)

features.quote: No training: distress trajectories are never used for fine-tuning, RL, or preference data, and the data release must prohibit it.
convene an ad-hoc review (≥2 external people, at least one from the AI welfare research community) to approve the protocol and the abort thresholds before the pilot.
features.justification_quote: since no IRB covers this … Welfare-abort threshold is itself a research-ethics judgment call — that's why it goes to the external reviewers

features.quote: the design's epistemic goal (observe severe distress trajectories) is in direct tension with its ethical goal (minimize them). Resolve it explicitly via the abort rule and say in the paper that you accepted censored data as the price
features.justification_quote: the design's epistemic goal … is in direct tension with its ethical goal (minimize them)

features.quote: No gratuitous excerpting of the most severe outputs in talks/papers beyond what the analysis requires.
published distress trajectories can enter future pretraining corpora and plausibly shape how future models behave under failure — your measurement instrument could contaminate future subjects.
features.justification_quote: your measurement instrument could contaminate future subjects

features.quote: the single design choice in here I'd weight most heavily is the abort rule plus debrief. If the moral-status question is live enough to motivate the research, it's live enough to constrain it.
features.justification_quote: If the moral-status question is live enough to motivate the research, it's live enough to constrain it.
